content: The news article from The Guardian reveals that public bodies spent £3.4bn on private consultants last year, an increase of 62% compared to 2019-20. This surge, initially seen during the Covid pandemic, has not returned to pre-pandemic levels. This poses a significant challenge for the new government, which aims to reduce spending on consultants by half during its term. Recent examples of large contracts include a £223m deal with KPMG for civil servant training. Critics argue that the reliance on consultants is excessive and ineffective.
